summary: Join our training course on conflict sensitivity in community development projects. Gain essential skills to navigate challenges and foster positive outcomes.
lede: Conflict Sensitivity in Community Development Projects helps professionals understand local tensions, power dynamics, stakeholders, and potential risks before they undermine a project. You will learn to identify conflict drivers, recognize do-no-harm concerns, and adapt project decisions to avoid increasing division, resentment, or risk. Through practical, scenario-based learning, the course supports professionals delivering social programs, infrastructure, livelihood initiatives, or humanitarian aid. Build a disciplined approach to spotting early warning signs, managing tensions, and delivering community projects with greater awareness of their wider context.
audienceIntro: This course is crafted for professionals working in, with, and around communities where tensions, grievances, or competition over resources may exist.
audience: Field coordinators and community outreach officers
Program designers and proposal developers for donor-funded
Social safeguards, resettlement, and stakeholder engagement specialists
modules: Foundations of Conflict Sensitivity in Community Projects
Project Design Through a Conflict-Sensitive Lens
Operational Decisions That Can Fuel or Reduce Tension
Conflict Sensitivity in Fragile, High-Risk, or Politicized Environments
Early Warning, Risk Management, and Scenario Planning
Integrating Conflict Sensitivity into Monitoring, Learning, and Reporting
Action Planning: Applying Conflict Sensitivity to Your Own Projects
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of project management and experience working in community development or related fields. Familiarity with stakeholder engagement and risk management concepts is beneficial.
